Testimony of Lt. Bruce Scott
NFNA LD 2053

An Act to Improve Safety by Allowing the Use of Variable-
message Signs on Public Service Vehicles
Senator Nangle, Rep. Crafts, and distinguished Members of the joint
Standing Committee on Transportation, my name is Lt. Bruce Scott, and I am the Commanding Officer of the State Police Traffic Safety Unit. I am here today to testify on behalf of the Department of Public Safety and the Maine State Police NFNA LD 2053.
This bill seeks to allow the use of variable message signs on "Public Service Vehicles." The original language of the bill would allow the use
of variable message signs on public service vehicles when the vehicles
are engaged in roadside repairs or recovery type services. However, the bill doesn't go far enough to restrict the misuse or abuse of these devices. The current bill doesn't restrict the type of public service vehicle that can be equipped with and display a variable message sign, the size of the sign, color of the lights used to create the message, the
direction that the sign may face, nor does it regulate the type of language that may be displayed.

create the standards not addressed by law, we would be able offer our
support of this bill.

For these reasons, we are Neither for Nor Against LD 2053.

On behalf of the Department of Public Safety and the Maine State
Police, I thank you for your time and would be happy to try and
answer any questions that you might have.

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation, thank you for the opportunity to testify today. My name is Dan Goodman, and I am the Manager of Public Affairs and Traffic Safety for AAA Northern New England. AAA serves more than one million members across Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont, AAA actively advocates for public policies that make New Hampshire a safer place to live, work, and raise a
family. Today, I come before you in support in LD 2047: An Act to Improve Safety by Allowing
the Use of Variable-message Signs on Public Service Vehicles.
Each year, AAA responds to approximately 250,000 roadside assistance calls in Maine. Every
one of those calls places a tow truck operator or roadside professional on the shoulder of a road often just feet from fast-moving traffic on the Maine Turnpike, l-95, Route 1, and countless rural highways. Maine's largely rural roadways, high speed limits, limited lighting, and frequent nighttime and winter conditions create especially dangerous environments for
roadside workers.

LD 2047 provides clear authority for authorized public service vehicles, including tow trucks, to use variable-message signs while stationary and actively engaged in roadside repair, vehicle recovery, or traffic control. For AAA and our contracted service providers, this means being able to use clear, highly visible messaging to warn approaching drivers that roadside professionals are present and that they need to slow down and move over
The safety need is well documented. AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety research found that
nearly 2,000 people were killed outside of a vehicle in roadside crashes between 2017 and 2021. Between 2015 and 2021, at least 123 roadside assistance providers were struck and killed while doing theirjobs. On average, 24 emergency responders, including tow truck operators, are killed each year about one every other week.

The good news is that variable message signs are a proven, effective safety countermeasure.
The AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety research shows that when these message signs are
active:

� Drivers are significantly more likely to slow down and move over
v The odds of a vehicle moving over increased to 95 percent 0 Speed reductions were greatest in the lane closest to the roadside vehicle 0 Vehicles that did change lanes tended to do so at lower speeds

The research clearly indicates that variable message signs positively influence driver behavior and should be strongly considered to protect roadside workers.
Similar laws have already been adopted successfully in 45 other states. For AAA and our service
providers, this legislation would allow us to equip our tow trucks with additional toolsto warn approaching drivers earlier and more clearly. For the public, it means fewer crashes, fewer
injuries, and safer travel for everyone. AAA respectfully urges the Committee to support this legislation and help ensure that those who assist stranded motorists on Maine's roads can return home safely at the end of their shift.

Testimony of lake Lachance, Executive Director, Maine Better Transportation Assoc.
Before the loint Standing Committee on Transportation In Support of

Ianuary 15"` , 2026
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Ioint Standing
Committee on Transportation. My name is Iake Lachance and I am testifying today on behalf of my employer, the Maine Better Transportation Association, in support of LD 2053, An Act to Improve Safety by Allowing the Use of Variable-Message Signs on Public
Service Vehicles
MBTA is a statewide coalition with a diverse membership including members who plan,
design, build, maintain, or use our transportation system. These include transportation contractors, engineers and suppliers, bus and rail companies, airports, marine and port interests, municipalities, and others committed to investing in our multimodal transportation infrastructure to boost the state's economy and quality of life.
This bill helps address a real and growing safety concern on Maine's roads and offers a
practical solution: drivers are being given every opportunity to know the environment they
are about to be in when traveling on our roads. We know the stories all too well, as recently
as this very week. This committee just heard testimony about authorizing a memorial highway for Deputy Luke Gross. These incidents are not isolated, and the risk continues to increase as traffic volumes rise and driver distraction becomes more common.
Variable-message signs are already a proven traffic safety tool. They provide clear, immediate, and adaptable communication to motorists--warning of stopped vehicles, lane restrictions, recovery operations, or hazardous conditions ahead. Allowing their use on
authorized public service vehicles when those vehicles are stationary and engaged in roadside work adds another layer of protection where it is most needed: directly at the
point of danger.

Importantly, this legislation is limited and practical. It does not require the purchase or use of new equipment. It simply gives public service vehicles the option to use variablemessage signs when appropriate. Local agencies, utilities, and public safety operators can
decide when and how this tool makes sense for their operations.
The bill also maintains proper oversight by allowing the Commissioner of Public Safety to adopt routine technical rules, ensuring consistent and responsible use.
At its core, this is a commonsense safety measure. Better information for drivers means better compliance, slower speeds, and more awareness---conditions that save lives. Giving
public service operators another tool to protect themselves and the traveling public is a reasonable and necessary step.
For these reasons, I respectfully urge the Committee to support this bill.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Good morning, Senator Nangle and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Transportation. My name is Lydia Crafts, and I represent House District 46, which
includes Bristol, Damariscotta, Monhegan Plantation, Newcastle and Nobleboro.
Today, I am pleased to present LD 2053, An Act to Improve Safety by Allowing
the Use of Variable-message Signs on Public Service Vehicles.

This policy adjusts Section 29-A to allow for the use of variable message boards
alerting the public to information regarding driving conditions (congestion,
accidents, maintenance, weather, etc). I have worked with the Departments of
Public Safety and Transportation along with AAA to find language that satisfies
the intent of the bill while maintaining safe roads and enforceable policies.

You will hear more from stakeholders about the bill's intent and implementation
and the amended language. Thank you for your consideration and I am happy to
answer any questions.
